## 5. Example HCL: KV v2 in `admin/platform`

```hcl
# Generated by vault-brownfield-codifier
# Capability: secrets-engines
# Doc ref: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs

resource "vault_mount" "admin_platform_secret" {
  provider    = vault.platform
  path        = "secret"
  type        = "kv"
  description = "Platform KV v2 secrets engine"

  options = {
    version = "2"
  }
}

resource "vault_kv_secret_backend_v2" "admin_platform_secret" {
  provider     = vault.platform
  mount        = vault_mount.admin_platform_secret.path
  max_versions = 10
  cas_required = false
}
```

```hcl
import {
  to = vault_mount.admin_platform_secret
  id = "secret"
}

import {
  to = vault_kv_secret_backend_v2.admin_platform_secret
  id = "secret/config"
}
```

`max_versions` and `cas_required` carry the values returned by
`GET /v1/secret/config`; the numbers above are illustrative. Omit
`delete_version_after` when it is `0s`.

### Zero-TTL omission

Vault reports `default_lease_ttl = 0` and `max_lease_ttl = 0` to mean "use the
system default". Emitting `default_lease_ttl_seconds = 0` makes the provider
send an explicit zero and can produce a perpetual diff against a mount that
inherits the system value. Therefore the generator checks each TTL field and
**omits it when it equals 0**. The same rule applies to every `*_ttl_seconds`
mount attribute.
